1

Signing in

Everyone starts here. Pick the role you were given, then your username and password.

  1. 1
    Choose your role — Admin, Auditor or Auditee. The line under the buttons changes to say what that role can do
  2. 2
    Username — the email address the account was created with
  3. 3
    Password — at least 8 characters, with a capital, a digit and a symbol
  4. 4
    Secure Sign In — goes to the second step below
  5. 5
    Create Account — for a new user, covered in step 3
  6. 6
    Forgot Password? — resets it using your authenticator app

If sign-in is refused, check the role first. An auditor account signed in on the Admin tab is the commonest reason a correct password appears to fail.

2

The two-factor code

After the password, the system asks for a six-digit code from your authenticator app. It changes every thirty seconds, so if one is refused, wait for the next rather than retyping the same digits.

Lost your authenticator? An administrator resets it. There is no way past this step, which is deliberate on a system holding audit evidence.

3

Creating an account

Choose the role first, then the username and password you want. Your authenticator is set up the first time you sign in.

You cannot change your own role. If you need a different one, an administrator has to grant it.

4

Resetting a forgotten password

Reset uses your authenticator app rather than email, because the system runs offline and cannot send anything. Enter your username, the current six-digit code, and the new password.

5

Starting an audit

Every audit lives in a session. This appears when you sign in, and whenever you press New Audit Session.

  1. 1
    Target framework — the standard being audited. ISO 27001 carries 93 controls; the other seven frameworks have their own
  2. 2
    Client / company name — optional, and it appears on the exported report
  3. 3
    Session title — filled in from the framework and the date; edit it if you run several audits for one client
  4. 4
    Create Session — opens the workspace
6

The workspace

Where most of the work happens: evidence on the left, scope on the right, and the run button at the bottom.

  1. 1
    New Audit Session — starts a fresh one; the current session is kept
  2. 2
    Analysis mode — how deeply each control is examined, see step 7
  3. 3
    Evidence drop zone — drag files in or browse. PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PPTX, HTML, JSON, TXT, PNG, JPG and ZIP are all read, screenshots included
  4. 4
    Target framework — what you chose when the session was created
  5. 5
    Scope detection method — how the controls get chosen, see step 8
  6. 6
    Target controls to audit — the list itself, grouped by clause
  7. 7
    Run Audit Scan — starts the run. Nothing is evaluated until you press it
7

Choosing how deep to go

The three modes trade time against thoroughness on the same evidence.

  1. 1
    Scanner — fastest. Reports what the evidence contains without judging whether a control is met
  2. 2
    Quick Audit — a judgement per control, with lighter checking
  3. 3
    Deep Audit — the full pipeline, including every grounding check before a finding is written. Slowest, and the one for a real audit
8

Attaching evidence

Evidence can be dropped in at any point before you run. Screenshots are read as well as documents, so a terminal capture works as proof.

  1. 1
    Already attached files — everything this session will read
  2. 2
    Browse files / Browse folder — or drag them onto the zone above
  3. 3
    Delete All — clears the session's evidence; the audit is not affected until you run again
9

Choosing which controls to audit

Three ways to decide what gets audited, and they produce different kinds of finding.

  1. 1
    Excel Upload — drop the scoping matrix and matching controls are selected for you. Each row can name its own policy and evidence files
  2. 2
    Manual Scope — tick controls yourself from the list
  3. 3
    Customize — question-based: you write the question, attach the evidence, and the answer is judged on that evidence alone

Excel and Manual expect both a policy and evidence for each control. Customize expects evidence only, so use it when you are answering a specific question rather than assessing a documented control.

10

Building a checklist by hand

If the client has no Excel scoping matrix, build the same thing here. Name the control, its policy, and the evidence that proves it is done.

  1. 1
    Control ID — optional. Leave it blank and the question is matched to a control automatically
  2. 2
    Policy document(s) — pick from the files you uploaded
  3. 3
    Evidence document(s) — the proof that the control is actually done
  4. 4
    Add row — one row per control; add as many as the audit needs
  5. 5
    Apply Checklist — selects those controls and locks each row to its files

Both sides are assessed and a row passes only if both hold. That is the difference from Customize scope, which judges on evidence alone. There is also a download a template link beside this button, which gives you excel_scoping_policy_evidence_template.xlsx to fill in offline and upload later.

11

Picking individual controls

Controls are grouped by clause. Open a clause to tick controls inside it; the counter beside each shows how many you have chosen.

  1. 1
    Search — type part of a name or number, such as 8.17 or clock
  2. 2
    Select All — every control in the framework
  3. 3
    Clear All — start again
12

Reading the findings

Findings appear here as the run progresses, and stay drafts until committed.

  1. 1
    Compliant / Non-compliant — running totals for this session
  2. 2
    Severity — P1 Critical through P4 Low
  3. 3
    Workflow status filter — narrow the list to what still needs attention
  4. 4
    Save to Shakthi DB — commits the findings to the permanent audit ledger
  5. 5
    Clear Draft Findings — discards them, leaving the ledger untouched

Nothing is permanent until you press Save to Shakthi DB. Each card shows the evidence it relied on, so the reasoning can be checked before it becomes part of the record.

13

Exporting and sending the report

Everything a finished audit produces. The preview underneath shows exactly what the PDF will contain before you generate it.

  1. 1
    Export Formal PDF Report — the client deliverable
  2. 2
    Export Editable Word Report — DOCX, when you want to edit before sending
  3. 3
    Download Raw CSV Dataset — every finding as data, for your own analysis
  4. 4
    Target auditee account — which auditee receives it
  5. 5
    Send Audit Findings to Client — delivers it inside the system, with no email involved
  6. 6
    Report metadata — firm, lead auditor, client and document ID, all of which appear on the report. Press Edit to change them

The report is empty until findings are committed. If it says no actionable findings, go back to Audit Records & Findings and press Save to Shakthi DB first.

14

Controls and backups

Custom controls, and backups of the audit ledger. Most auditors never open this tab; it is for whoever maintains the installation.
